thread:
Maria: heads-up — post-deploy smoke showed a small spike in p95 for embeddings on eu-west-1. not catastrophic but > our threshold. deploying a short safety-mutex so we can decide next steps
Jon: saw it. metrics look like a sparse tail, maybe odd traffic pattern. can we run a 10m throttled canary before doing anything heavy?
Kevin: +1 on canary but we need to prevent autopilot rollback from flipping while we debug. can we set `deploybot.safety_mutex` to `locked` for the release id?
deploy-bot: deploy-bot here — auto-rollback window is active for r=2026.03.21-0421. To suppress automatic rollback set `--safety-mutex locked` or use the web console.
Maria: I'm going to lock mutex for 15m. intention: let platform run a narrow canary (5% traffic) and check request distribution + kv cache hit rates. will update release notes if we pin version.
Tara: FYI we already drafted a short customer note in case we need a rollback. don’t send unless we actually pin/revert.
Jon: canary started: `traffic-split set r=2026.03.21-0421 5% -> variant-b`
Kevin: logs show a few backend async workers spiking in latency for long tail requests — correlates with certain embedding dims. i pushed a temporary kernel flag to stage to limit max_batch_size for that worker pool.
Maria: good. after 8m of canary p95 looks steady; eu-west-1 aggregate still ~12% over baseline but canary is fine. deploy-bot: what's the current rollback policy state?
deploy-bot: autopilot rollback is enabled. safety-mutex is locked by Maria until 1718904415. autopilot will not trigger while locked. manual rollback still permitted.
Jon: thinking: two options — manual rollback to v2.14.1 (fast) or keep pinned traffic and roll forward with a targeted kernel rollback on the worker pool. which has less blast radius?
Kevin: manual rollback will restore stable latency immediately but loses some routing optimizations we just shipped. targeted kernel rollback is lower blast but risk remaining undetected pop spikes. my recommendation: pin traffic (stop further ramp), notify customers, and roll kernel-backed fix to canary then to 20% then 50%.
Maria: agree with Kevin. i'll update release notes and send a short internal comm to support + eng on rotation. Tara, can you patch the customer-facing blurb?
Tara: on it. short blurb: "We're monitoring a small latency regression for embeddings; no data loss. We're deploying a targeted fix and may briefly roll back if we see customer impact." will share link in 5m.
Maria: locking mutex extended for another 10m while we complete the staged rollout. leaving autopilot suppressed.
Kevin: executing targeted rollout now: `ops run rollout --pool=embed-workers-eu --image=kernel-fix-7 --slice=canary`
Jon: telemetry looks good at 20% and 50%. p95 trending down toward baseline.
Maria: consensus then — no full rollback. plan: keep safety-mutex locked until the kernel fix hits 100% and we monitor 30m. I'll unpin mutex and re-enable autopilot after that.
deploy-bot: noted. will resume autopilot at 1718906215 unless manually changed.
Kevin: leaving a short runbook note in the release thread: 1) safety-mutex locked -> avoid autopilot flip; 2) targeted kernel rollout succeeded; 3) no manual rollback executed; 4) follow-up: add an embedding-dim histogram to our perf dashboard.
Maria: thanks team. sending summary to #product and #support now. :thumbsup:
Tara: posted customer blurb: https://company.docs/release-notes/2026-03-21-embed-latency
